subject: Request: Conditional quarterly invoicing + one-time onboarding credit
messages:
From: Samantha Flores <samantha.flores@medflow.io>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Carlos Ruiz <c.ruiz@medflow.io>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Billing cadence ask for MedFlow pilot

Hi Hannah —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We’re excited to pilot Redwood for our patient-scheduling flows. Quick ask from Finance: to help align with our budgeting windows, can we do quarterly invoicing for the first six months (invoices issued at the end of each quarter) instead of monthly?

Separately, our AP team requested a one-time onboarding credit (30% of month-one invoice) to offset integration costs. Finally, for the pilot cashflow we’d like Net-90 on the first two invoices, then revert to standard Net-30.

I’ve attached the signed SOW (v2) and an AP contact scan — happy to get a formal PO after we lock terms. Can you route this for exec/finance approval?

Thanks,
Samantha Flores
Head of Partnerships
MedFlow Health
attachments: MedFlow_SOW_v2.pdf, MedFlow_AP_Approval_Scan.jpg
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Billing cadence ask for MedFlow pilot — need deal desk / exec guidance

Team — forwarding MedFlow’s request. Key asks: quarterly invoicing for 6 months, one-time 30% onboarding credit, Net-90 for first two invoices. SOW attached.

My read: we can be flexible on cadence for a pilot if we protect cash — prefer prepay or escrow, but MedFlow is asking for credit + extended terms which increases receivables risk.

Can we get quick takes: 1) are we comfortable approving Net-90 for two invoices with that credit? 2) acceptable guardrails (usage holdback, shorter pilot limit, PO pre-req)? 3) if approved, what sign-off level needed (finance vs. exec)?

I’ll coordinate response to MedFlow once we align.

— Hannah
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 12:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Billing cadence ask for MedFlow pilot — need deal desk / exec guidance

Hannah —

I’m okay with conditional quarterly invoicing for a pilot but not with an unconditional Net-90 + 30% credit. Proposed compromise:

- Approve quarterly invoicing for two quarters only (trial period).
- One-time onboarding credit limited to 30% of the first invoice, to be earned only after completion of onboarding milestones (KB integration + 2 successful inference runs).
- Net-90 for up to 60 days (i.e., convert to Net-60) unless we receive a signed PO and payment schedule. Alternatively, accept Net-90 but require an AP contact verification form and a payment security (ACH authorization) on file.

If MedFlow can provide a PO before the first quarterly invoice, we can be more flexible. If they can’t, we need a finance exec sign-off — I can take this to finance leadership for a final OK if you want.

-Jonas
Head of Revenue Operations
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Billing cadence ask for MedFlow pilot — need deal desk / exec guidance

Hannah / Jonas —

Risk perspective: MedFlow is mid-market, decent credit history but limited enterprise track record. We can do a time-limited concession with these controls:

- Limit quarterly invoicing to Q3/Q4 2027 (two quarters), after which billing reverts to monthly Net-30.
- One-time onboarding credit of 30% applied to month-one invoice, recoupable if pilot is canceled within 45 days (credit clawback language in SOW).
- Require signed PO before we issue the first quarterly invoice OR require a 25% prepayment of the first quarter.
- Finance approval required for Net-90; I can approve Net-60 at my level. Net-90 requires CFO sign-off.

If the commercial team is comfortable pushing PO/prepay, I’ll approve the conditional terms (Net-60 + credit + quarterly for two quarters). Otherwise route to CFO for Net-90.
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Flores <samantha.flores@medflow.io>, MedFlow Finance <ap@medflow.io>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 15:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Billing cadence ask for MedFlow pilot — decision and conditional approval

Samantha / Carlos —

Thanks for the note and for the SOW. Quick update from Redwood: we’re prepared to accommodate a pilot billing cadence change with these conditions (approved by Finance):

1) Quarterly invoicing limited to two quarters only (Q3 & Q4 2027), after which we revert to monthly Net-30.
2) One-time onboarding credit of 30% applied to the first invoice — the credit is contingent on completion of onboarding milestones outlined in SOW. If the pilot is canceled within 45 days of invoice issuance, the credit will be recouped (clawback).
3) Net-60 is approved at Redwood finance level for the invoices in question. Net-90 requires CFO sign-off and is not approved at this stage.
4) Prior to issuing the first quarterly invoice, we require either: a) a signed PO referencing the SOW, or b) a 25% prepayment of the first quarter. AP contact form attached for your convenience.

Next steps: please confirm whether you can provide a PO or would prefer the prepayment route. Once we have that, I’ll issue the revised SOW and an invoice schedule. Attached: updated SOW (redline-ready) and AP form.

Appreciate the partnership — we want to make the pilot smooth while managing mutual risk.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
+hannah_schmitt@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192
